value: root length, number of lateral roots, biomass and relative shoot area significantly increased under the static magnetic field compared with sham
method: seedlings on half-strength MS medium under a static magnetic field from NdFeB N38 magnets for 7 days, compared with sham; total root length, lateral root number, fresh whole-plant biomass and relative shoot area scored; one-way ANOVA
conditions: Col-0; the effect came from one of five magnet setups screened (10 cm regular triangular prism magnet with its edge perpendicular to gravity, inhomogeneous field); thin cuboid (about 5 mT), thick cuboid (about 200 mT), 3 cm prism and 10 cm prism edge parallel to gravity gave no significant effect; 22 C, 16 h light 8 h dark; three independent experiments, n = 24 seedlings; 'all conditions' means Sham, SMF, Sham + Fe and SMF + Fe, and iron stress alone lowered root length, biomass and shoot area; field strengths are given only for the parallel placement (about 150 mT 5 mm above the edge), none for the perpendicular placement that worked; the 3 cm prism was never tested perpendicular; Fe stress was 300 uM FeSO4

source.authors: Zhou X, Zhang L, Zhang P, Xu H, Song J, Chang Y, Cai T, Xie C
source.title: Comparative transcriptomic analysis revealed important processes underlying the static magnetic field effects on Arabidopsis

where: frontiersin.org full-text article page, Results; sentence returned in two consecutive pieces (split after 'significantly increased') on two fetches
quote: Interestingly, the root lengths, amount of lateral root, biomass and relative shoot area are all significantly increased upon magnetic field treatment, compared with the sham groups in all conditions.
